etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English soleyn, from Anglo-Norman soleyn (“alone”), from Old French sole (“single, sole, alone”), from Latin sōlus (“by oneself alone”). The change in meaning from "single" to morose occurred in Middle English.
senses: Having a brooding ill temper; sulky.
(archaic) One who is solitary, or lives alone; a hermit.
(in the plural) Sullen feelings or manners; sulks; moroseness.
